subject: KMS rotation appendix & keystore proof exchange - Hendrix request
messages:
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@hendrix-fin.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@hendrix-fin.com
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KMS/HSM evidence request - initial items

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. Hendrix is preparing for a focused control review next week and our security team needs a small artifact bundle to validate key management and rotation controls for your tenant. Can you provide the following by EOD Wed (2028-08-23)?

- Sample rotation logs (audit lines with timestamps, key IDs, operator IDs) covering one rotation event
- HSM attestation (serial / vendor statement) used to protect master keys
- Statement on whether rotated logs or exports contain any plaintext key material (yes/no + short explanation)
- TLS/transit cipher-suite summary for inter-service traffic and any mutual-TLS usages
- A signed attestation from an authorized Redwood security contact that the provided artifacts are representative (not full production key material)

If you prefer, a password-protected ZIP with sample files on a shared Drive link is fine — we just need clear provenance for the items above.

Contact for tech clarifications: security@hendrix-fin.com.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,

Alyssa Greene
Senior Security Analyst
Hendrix Financial

--

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@hendrix-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence request - initial items

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the list and timeline. Looping in Marissa (security & compliance ops) and Jonas (crypto lead) so we can assemble a concise appendix rather than sending raw exports.

High level notes up front:
- We will not send any plaintext key material. Samples will be redacted and/or sampled with identifiers.
- We can provide HSM attestation (vendor PPT + serial) and a signed attestation from our security lead.
- Rotation logs will be exported as a CSV sample with operator IDs replaced by opaque employee IDs; timestamps and key IDs will be real and time-ordered.
- Transport cipher-suite summary will be included (TLS 1.2/1.3 usage matrix + mutual-TLS endpoints).

Marissa / Jonas — can you confirm expected artifacts and whether we should include a short README describing redaction rules? Alyssa — we'll post a Drive folder with password-protected artifacts and share the link here.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0162

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@hendrix-fin.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence request - initial items (artifact bundle)

Hi Alyssa / Tessa,

I've prepared a small appendix and placed sampled artifacts in a read-only Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bKMSProofsExample

Contents (sampled / redacted):
- kms-rotation-log-sample.csv (CSV; contains key_id,event_type,timestamp,actor_id where actor_id is an opaque internal id; we retained exact timestamps & key_id prefixes)
- hsm-attestation-serial-2028.pdf (vendor attestation with serial numbers visible; no key material)
- transport-tls-cipher-suite.txt (list of service pairs and selected cipher suites; indicates TLS 1.3 preferred, mTLS used for control plane)
- README-redaction.txt (describes redaction policy used and fields removed)

Notes:
- The sampled rotation log is a representative sequence for an automated rotation event; it does NOT include wrapped key payloads or any unencrypted key material.
- HSM attestation is a vendor-signed statement; we are providing a redacted copy here.
- We can provide a signed attestation PDF from Redwood security (signed-attestation-hendrix-20280822.pdf) once Alyssa confirms the content template you need.

Attachment stubs referenced above are included in the Drive folder. If you need the files delivered via SFTP or a different mechanism, let me know.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: kms-rotation-log-sample.csv; hsm-attestation-serial-2028.pdf; transport-tls-cipher-suite.txt

--

From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@hendrix-fin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence request - initial items (artifact bundle)

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications before we accept the appendix into our review:
1) Can you confirm in writing that none of the CSV samples or PDFs contain any plaintext (unencrypted) secret material or key values? We need explicit language for our auditors.
2) Will the signed attestation state the person signing and their authority (title + binding statement)?
3) For the rotation log CSV, can you confirm whether the key IDs are the full KMS key names or truncated prefixes? We need to map rotation events to our control matrix.

If you can answer 1–3 and post the signed attestation we will proceed.

Regards,

Alyssa Greene
Senior Security Analyst
Hendrix Financial

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@hendrix-fin.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence request - initial items (artifact bundle)

Hi Alyssa — answers inline.

1) Explicit confirmation: NONE of the provided artifact files contain plaintext or unwrapped key material. The rotation CSV contains metadata about rotation events (timestamps, event_type, key_id prefix) and operator identifiers that have been pseudonymized. The HSM attestation is a vendor-signed statement and contains no key material. The transport summary is configuration metadata only.

2) Yes — the signed attestation will be delivered as signed-attestation-hendrix-20280822.pdf. It will be signed by me (Marissa Cole, Security & Compliance Operations Manager) and will include the following binding language: "I attest that the artifacts provided are representative samples of Redwood Inference key management and rotation records, and do not contain plaintext cryptographic key material or private key values." If you need legal-level language, we can route the attestation to our Head of Security for a co-signed statement.

3) Key IDs in the CSV are truncated to the stable key prefix (first 12 characters) sufficient to correlate events without exposing full key ARNs. If you need a fuller mapping for control reconciliation we can provide additional context under an NDA and via secure SFTP.

I've uploaded the signed attestation to the Drive folder (signed-attestation-hendrix-20280822.pdf). HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/ticket/REDWOOD-15892 for traceability.

Please confirm receipt and whether you need anything else for the review.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: signed-attestation-hendrix-20280822.pdf

--
